answer: A dune shifts with every wind, but a horizon stays put: an identity gains standing only by proving presence in widely separated places over time, verified by independent local witnesses who have no reason to collude. An atlas of these proofs is public, so a Sybil farm, thousands of identities all proving presence from the same data center, stands out immediately. Faking one location is easy; faking a hundred uncorrelated ones, each attested by strangers, costs more than the attack returns.
